summary: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says.
takeaways: Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none.
As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does.
Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text.
